title: int2str
summary: Convert rounded integer values to a character array in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Accepts GPU tensors but gathers them to host memory before rounding and formatting.

description: `int2str(N)` treats `N` as a numeric or logical scalar, vector, or matrix, rounds floating-point values to integers, and returns a MATLAB `char` array.
behaviors: Floating-point values are rounded before conversion.
Scalar and vector inputs return one text row; matrix inputs return one character row per numeric row.
Columns are padded with spaces so each textual column aligns across rows.
Logical and integer inputs are accepted and formatted as numeric 0/1 or integer values.
GPU tensors are gathered to host memory before formatting.
Empty inputs return a `0x0` character array.
Complex inputs, inputs with more than two dimensions, and non-numeric inputs raise descriptive errors.

faqs.question: How is `int2str` different from `num2str`?
faqs.answer: `int2str` rounds numeric values to integers first and has no precision or format-string arguments. Use `num2str` when you need decimal formatting or explicit `printf`-style control.

faqs.question: Does `int2str` return a modern string scalar?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB `int2str` returns a character array. Wrap the result with `string(...)` if you need a string scalar.

faqs.question: Does `int2str` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. GPU inputs are accepted, gathered to host memory, and formatted on the CPU, matching MATLAB's documented GPU-array limitation.

faqs.question: Does `int2str` support complex inputs?
faqs.answer: No. RunMat rejects complex inputs for `int2str` because MATLAB documents the input as a numeric matrix of integer values and does not document complex formatting for this function.

points: `N` is a numeric or logical scalar, vector, or matrix.
Floating-point values are rounded before text conversion.
Returns `chr`, a MATLAB `char` array with matrix columns padded for alignment.
